:::{#thm-prediction-error}
#### Expected squared prediction error

Let $\Outvar_0 = \targetfnf{\predvar_0} + \noise$,
where $\targetfn$ is a fixed function,
$\noise$, the noise in the output at $\predvar_0$, has $\E{\noise} = 0$ and $\Var{\noise} = \varpar$,
and $\noise$ is independent of the prediction $\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}$,
which has $\E{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}^2} < \infty$.
Then

$$\E{\paren{\Outvar_0 - \etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}^2} = \sqf{\bias{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}} + \Var{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}} + \varpar$$

:::

::: proof

Write $D \eqdef \targetfnf{\predvar_0} - \etargetfnf{\predvar_0}$.

First, the prediction error in terms of $\noise$ and $D$:

$$
\ba
\Outvar_0 - \etargetfnf{\predvar_0}
&= \paren{\targetfnf{\predvar_0} + \noise} - \etargetfnf{\predvar_0}
&& \text{(definition of } \Outvar_0 \text{)} \\
&= \noise + \paren{\targetfnf{\predvar_0} - \etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}
&& \text{(reorder the terms of the sum)} \\
&= \noise + D
&& \text{(definition of } D \text{)}
\ea
$$

Next, expand the square and split the expectation.
The last two steps use
[linearity of expectation](expectation.qmd#thm-linearity-expectation),
first for the expectation of a sum and then for a constant factor:

$$
\ba
\E{\paren{\Outvar_0 - \etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}^2}
&= \E{\paren{\noise + D}^2}
&& \text{(the error above)} \\
&= \E{\noise^2 + 2 \noise D + D^2}
&& \text{(expand: } \paren{a + b}^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2 \text{)} \\
&= \E{\noise^2} + \E{2 \noise D} + \E{D^2}
&& \text{(expectation of a sum)} \\
&= \E{\noise^2} + 2\E{\noise D} + \E{D^2}
&& \text{(constant factor 2)}
\ea
$$

Each of the three terms is evaluated in turn.

- The noise term is $\E{\noise^2} = \varpar$,
  by @sol-noise-second-moment.
- For the cross term,
  $\noise$ is independent of $\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}$,
  hence of $D$,
  because $\targetfnf{\predvar_0}$ is a constant.
  So the expectation of the product is the product of the expectations:

  $$
  \ba
  \E{\noise D}
  &= \E{\noise}\E{D}
  && \text{(independence)} \\
  &= 0 \cdot \E{D}
  && \text{(} \E{\noise} = 0 \text{)} \\
  &= 0
  && \text{(zero times a number)}
  \ea
  $$

- For the last term,
  @thm-variance gives $\E{D^2} = \Var{D} + \sqf{\E{D}}$.
  The mean of $D$ is

  $$
  \ba
  \E{D}
  &= \E{\targetfnf{\predvar_0}} - \E{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}
  && \text{(expectation of a difference)} \\
  &= \targetfnf{\predvar_0} - \E{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}
  && \text{(} \targetfnf{\predvar_0} \text{ is a constant)} \\
  &= -\paren{\E{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}} - \targetfnf{\predvar_0}}
  && \text{(factor out } -1 \text{)} \\
  &= -\bias{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}
  && \text{(definition of bias)}
  \ea
  $$

  so $\sqf{\E{D}} = \sqf{\bias{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}}$,
  because $\sqf{\paren{-a}} = \sqf{a}$.
  The variance of $D$ is

  $$
  \ba
  \Var{D}
  &= \E{\sqf{\paren{D - \E{D}}}}
  && \text{(definition of variance)} \\
  &= \E{\sqf{\paren{-\paren{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0} - \E{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}}}}}
  && \text{(substitute } D \text{ and } \E{D} \text{; the constant } \targetfnf{\predvar_0} \text{ cancels)} \\
  &= \E{\sqf{\paren{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0} - \E{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}}}}
  && \text{(} \sqf{\paren{-a}} = \sqf{a} \text{)} \\
  &= \Var{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}
  && \text{(definition of variance)}
  \ea
  $$

Substituting the three terms into the expansion gives

$$
\ba
\E{\paren{\Outvar_0 - \etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}^2}
&= \varpar + 2 \cdot 0 + \paren{\Var{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}} + \sqf{\bias{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}}}
&& \text{(the three terms above)} \\
&= \sqf{\bias{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}} + \Var{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}} + \varpar
&& \text{(drop } 2 \cdot 0 \text{, reorder the terms)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-irreducible-error}
#### Irreducible error

In @thm-prediction-error,
the term $\varpar = \Var{\noise}$ is the **irreducible error**.
It does not depend on the prediction $\etargetfn$,
so no choice of prediction can remove it.
The theorem concerns the single point $\predvar_0$,
so $\varpar$ may differ from one point to another:
it does not assume constant noise variance across points.
For example, in @exr-prediction-error, $\varpar = 3$,
so every prediction there has expected squared error at least $3$.

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

This expected prediction error decomposition into squared bias, variance, and irreducible error follows @james2021islr2e [Section 2.2.2].

:::
